prusa.automatic_extrusion_widths.label: Automatic extrusion widths calculation
prusa.automatic_extrusion_widths.tooltip: Automatically calculates extrusion widths based on the nozzle diameter of the currently used extruder. This setting is essential for printing with different nozzle diameters.

prusa.avoid_crossing_curled_overhangs.label: Avoid crossing curled overhangs (Experimental)
prusa.avoid_crossing_curled_overhangs.tooltip: Plan travel moves such that the extruder avoids areas where the filament may be curled up. This is mostly happening on steeper rounded overhangs and may cause a crash with the nozzle. This feature slows down both the print and the G-code generation.

prusa.bed_temperature_extruder.label: Bed temperature by extruder
prusa.bed_temperature_extruder.tooltip: The extruder which determines bed temperatures. Set to 0 to determine temperatures based on the first printing extruder of the first and the second layers.

prusa.over_bridge_speed.label: Over bridges
prusa.over_bridge_speed.tooltip: Speed for printing solid infill above bridges. Set to 0 to use solid infill speed. If set as percentage, the speed is calculated over solid infill speed.

prusa.enable_dynamic_fan_speeds.label: Enable dynamic fan speeds
prusa.enable_dynamic_fan_speeds.tooltip: This setting enables dynamic fan speed control on overhangs.

prusa.colorprint_heights.label: Colorprint height
prusa.colorprint_heights.tooltip: Heights at which a filament change is to occur.

prusa.compatible_printers_condition_cumm.provenance: Ported from PrusaSlicer@b028299:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:963 (label generated from the key)

prusa.compatible_prints_condition_cummul.label: Compatible prints condition cummulative
prusa.compatible_prints_condition_cummul.provenance: Ported from PrusaSlicer@b028299:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:966 (label generated from the key)

prusa.cooling.label: Enable auto cooling
prusa.cooling.tooltip: This flag enables the automatic cooling logic that adjusts print speed and fan speed according to layer printing time.

prusa.cooling_slowdown_logic.label: Cooling slowdown logic
prusa.cooling_slowdown_logic.tooltip: Determines how the printer slows down layer printing when the minimum layer time isn't reached. 'Consistent surface' first tries to preserve the print speeds of the first two perimeters by slowing all other features. Only if this isn't sufficient, it also slows down those first two perimeters. 'Uniform cooling' slows down all print features, including the first two perimeters.

prusa.cooling_perimeter_transition_dista.label: Perimeter transition distance
prusa.cooling_perimeter_transition_dista.tooltip: Distance in millimeters before non-slowed perimeters where the original unslowed print speed is restored. This reduces print quality issues when transitioning from heavily slowed feature to fast perimeter printing.

prusa.duplicate_distance.label: Distance between copies
prusa.duplicate_distance.tooltip: Distance used for the auto-arrange feature of the plater.

prusa.extra_perimeters.label: Extra perimeters if needed
prusa.extra_perimeters.tooltip: Add more perimeters when needed for avoiding gaps in sloping walls. Slic3r keeps adding perimeters, until more than 70% of the loop immediately above is supported.

prusa.extrusion_axis.label: Extrusion axis
prusa.extrusion_axis.tooltip: Use this option to set the axis letter associated to your printer's extruder (usually E but some printers use A).

prusa.filament_infill_max_speed.label: Max non-crossing infill speed
prusa.filament_infill_max_speed.tooltip: Maximum speed allowed for this filament while printing infill without any self intersections in a single layer. Set to zero for no limit.

prusa.filament_infill_max_crossing_speed.label: Max crossing infill speed
prusa.filament_infill_max_crossing_speed.tooltip: Maximum speed allowed for this filament while printing infill with self intersections in a single layer. Set to zero for no limit.

prusa.filament_purge_multiplier.label: Purge volume multiplier
prusa.filament_purge_multiplier.tooltip: Purging volume on the wipe tower is determined by 'multimaterial_purging' in Printer Settings. This option allows to modify the volume on filament level. Note that the project can override this by setting project-specific values.

prusa.filament_abrasive.label: Abrasive material
prusa.filament_abrasive.tooltip: This flag means that the material is abrasive and requires a hardened nozzle. The value is used by the printer to check it.

prusa.filament_spool_weight.label: Spool weight
prusa.filament_spool_weight.tooltip: Enter weight of the empty filament spool. One may weigh a partially consumed filament spool before printing and one may compare the measured weight with the calculated weight of the filament with the spool to find out whether the amount of filament on the spool is sufficient to finish the print.

prusa.filament_flush_volume.label: Flush volume
prusa.filament_flush_volume.tooltip: Volume of filament to flush during a tool change. Used in custom toolchange G-code.

prusa.filament_flush_speed.label: Flush speed
prusa.filament_flush_speed.tooltip: Extrusion speed used for flushing during a tool change. Used in custom toolchange G-code.

prusa.first_layer_acceleration_over_raft.label: First object layer over raft interface
prusa.first_layer_acceleration_over_raft.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for first layer of object above raft interface. Set zero to disable acceleration control for first layer of object above raft interface.

prusa.first_layer_speed_over_raft.label: Speed of object first layer over raft interface
prusa.first_layer_speed_over_raft.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to all the print moves of the first object layer above raft interface, regardless of their type. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will scale the default speeds.

prusa.gap_fill_enabled.label: Fill gaps
prusa.gap_fill_enabled.tooltip: Enables filling of gaps between perimeters and between the inner most perimeters and infill.

prusa.gcode_substitutions.label: G-code substitutions
prusa.gcode_substitutions.tooltip: Find / replace patterns in G-code lines and substitute them.

prusa.wipe_tower_acceleration.label: Wipe tower
prusa.wipe_tower_acceleration.tooltip: This is the acceleration your printer will use for wipe tower. Set zero to disable acceleration control for the wipe tower.

prusa.travel_short_distance_acceleration.label: Travel short distance acceleration
prusa.travel_short_distance_acceleration.tooltip: Acceleration used for short travel moves. Short travel distance is determined by the retract_before_travel setting.

prusa.infill_every_layers.label: Combine infill every n layers
prusa.infill_every_layers.tooltip: This feature allows to combine infill and speed up your print by extruding thicker infill layers while preserving thin perimeters, thus accuracy.

prusa.inherits_cummulative.label: Inherits cummulative
prusa.inherits_cummulative.provenance: Ported from PrusaSlicer@b028299:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:2060 (label generated from the key)

prusa.ironing.label: Enable ironing
prusa.ironing.tooltip: Enable ironing of the top layers with the hot print head for smooth surface

prusa.remaining_times.label: Supports remaining times
prusa.remaining_times.tooltip: Emit M73 P[percent printed] R[remaining time in minutes] at 1 minute intervals into the G-code to let the firmware show accurate remaining time. As of now only the Prusa i3 MK3 firmware recognizes M73. Also the i3 MK3 firmware supports M73 Qxx Sxx for the silent mode.

prusa.binary_gcode.label: Supports binary G-code
prusa.binary_gcode.tooltip: Enable, if the firmware supports binary G-code format (bgcode). To generate .bgcode files, make sure you have binary G-code enabled in Configuration->Preferences->Other.

prusa.machine_limits_usage.label: Purpose of Machine Limits
prusa.machine_limits_usage.tooltip: How to apply the Machine Limits

prusa.max_print_speed.label: Max print speed
prusa.max_print_speed.tooltip: When setting other speed settings to 0 Slic3r will autocalculate the optimal speed in order to keep constant extruder pressure. This experimental setting is used to set the highest print speed you want to allow.

prusa.max_volumetric_speed.label: Max volumetric speed
prusa.max_volumetric_speed.tooltip: This experimental setting is used to set the maximum volumetric speed your extruder supports.

prusa.max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slop.label: Max volumetric slope negative
prusa.max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slop.tooltip: This experimental setting is used to limit the speed of change in extrusion rate for a transition from higher speed to lower speed. A value of 1.8 mm³/s² ensures, that a change from the extrusion rate of 5.4 mm³/s (0.45 mm extrusion width, 0.2 mm extrusion height, feedrate 60 mm/s) to 1.8 mm³/s (feedrate 20 mm/s) will take at least 2 seconds.

prusa.multimaterial_purging.label: Purging volume
prusa.multimaterial_purging.tooltip: Determines purging volume on the wipe tower. This can be modified in Filament Settings ('filament_purge_multiplier') or overridden using project-specific settings.

prusa.physical_printer_settings_id.label: Physical printer settings id
prusa.physical_printer_settings_id.provenance: Ported from PrusaSlicer@b028299:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:2688 (label generated from the key)

prusa.gcode_resolution.label: G-code resolution
prusa.gcode_resolution.tooltip: Maximum deviation of exported G-code paths from their full resolution counterparts. Very high resolution G-code requires huge amount of RAM to slice and preview, also a 3D printer may stutter not being able to process a high resolution G-code in a timely manner. On the other hand, a low resolution G-code will produce a low poly effect and because the G-code reduction is performed at each layer independently, visible artifacts may be produced.

prusa.travel_ramping_lift.label: Use ramping lift
prusa.travel_ramping_lift.tooltip: Generates a ramping lift instead of lifting the extruder directly upwards. The travel is split into two phases: the ramp and the standard horizontal travel. This option helps reduce stringing.

prusa.travel_max_lift.label: Maximum ramping lift
prusa.travel_max_lift.tooltip: Maximum lift height of the ramping lift. It may not be reached if the next position is close to the old one.

prusa.travel_lift_before_obstacle.label: Steeper ramp before obstacles
prusa.travel_lift_before_obstacle.tooltip: If enabled, PrusaSlicer detects obstacles along the travel path and makes the slope steeper in case an obstacle might be hit during the initial phase of the travel.

prusa.nozzle_high_flow.label: High flow nozzle
prusa.nozzle_high_flow.tooltip: High flow nozzles allow higher print speeds.

prusa.scarf_seam_max_segment_length.label: Max scarf joint segment length
prusa.scarf_seam_max_segment_length.tooltip: Maximum length of any scarf joint segment.

prusa.seam_preferred_direction_jitter.label: Seam preferred direction jitter
prusa.seam_preferred_direction_jitter.tooltip: Preferred direction of the seam - jitter

prusa.solid_infill_every_layers.label: Solid infill every
prusa.solid_infill_every_layers.tooltip: This feature allows to force a solid layer every given number of layers. Zero to disable. You can set this to any value (for example 9999); Slic3r will automatically choose the maximum possible number of layers to combine according to nozzle diameter and layer height.

prusa.solid_layers.label: Solid layers
prusa.solid_layers.tooltip: Number of solid layers to generate on top and bottom surfaces.

prusa.solid_min_thickness.label: Minimum thickness of a top / bottom shell
prusa.solid_min_thickness.tooltip: Minimum thickness of a top / bottom shell

prusa.autoemit_temperature_commands.label: Emit temperature commands automatically
prusa.autoemit_temperature_commands.tooltip:
When enabled, PrusaSlicer will check whether your custom Start G-Code contains G-codes to set extruder, bed or chamber temperature (M104, M109, M140, M190, M141 and M191). If so, the temperatures will not be emitted automatically so you're free to customize the order of heating commands and other custom actions. Note that you can use placeholder variables for all PrusaSlicer settings, so you can put a "M109 S[first_layer_temperature]" command wherever you want.
If your custom Start G-Code does NOT contain these G-codes, PrusaSlicer will execute the Start G-Code after heated chamber was set to its temperature, bed reached its target temperature and extruder just started heating.

When disabled, PrusaSlicer will NOT emit commands to heat up extruder, bed or chamber, leaving all to Custom Start G-Code.

prusa.color_change_gcode.label: Color change G-code
prusa.color_change_gcode.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a code for the color change

prusa.support_material_closing_radius.label: Closing radius
prusa.support_material_closing_radius.tooltip: For snug supports, the support regions will be merged using morphological closing operation. Gaps smaller than the closing radius will be filled in.

prusa.support_material_synchronize_layer.label: Synchronize with object layers
prusa.support_material_synchronize_layer.tooltip: Synchronize support layers with the object print layers. This is useful with multi-material printers, where the extruder switch is expensive. This option is only available when top contact Z distance is set to zero.

prusa.support_material_with_sheath.label: With sheath around the support
prusa.support_material_with_sheath.tooltip: Add a sheath (a single perimeter line) around the base support. This makes the support more reliable, but also more difficult to remove.

prusa.support_tree_branch_diameter_doubl.label: Branch Diameter with double walls
prusa.support_tree_branch_diameter_doubl.tooltip: Branches with area larger than the area of a circle of this diameter will be printed with double walls for stability. Set this value to zero for no double walls.

prusa.use_volumetric_e.label: Use volumetric E
prusa.use_volumetric_e.tooltip: This experimental setting uses outputs the E values in cubic millimeters instead of linear millimeters. If your firmware doesn't already know filament diameter(s), you can put commands like 'M200 D[filament_diameter_0] T0' in your start G-code in order to turn volumetric mode on and use the filament diameter associated to the filament selected in Slic3r. This is only supported in recent Marlin.

prusa.variable_layer_height.label: Enable variable layer height feature
prusa.variable_layer_height.tooltip: Some printers or printer setups may have difficulties printing with a variable layer height. Enabled by default.

prusa.prefer_clockwise_movements.label: Prefer clockwise movements
prusa.prefer_clockwise_movements.tooltip: This setting makes the printer print loops clockwise instead of counterclockwise.

prusa.wiping_volumes_use_custom_matrix.label: Wiping volumes use custom matrix
prusa.wiping_volumes_use_custom_matrix.provenance: Ported from PrusaSlicer@b028299:src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp:3857 (label generated from the key)

prusa.filament_travel_max_lift.label: Maximum ramping lift
prusa.filament_travel_max_lift.tooltip: Maximum lift height of the ramping lift. It may not be reached if the next position is close to the old one.

prusa.filament_travel_lift_before_obstac.label: Steeper ramp before obstacles
prusa.filament_travel_lift_before_obstac.tooltip: If enabled, PrusaSlicer detects obstacles along the travel path and makes the slope steeper in case an obstacle might be hit during the initial phase of the travel.

prusa.filament_travel_ramping_lift.label: Use ramping lift
prusa.filament_travel_ramping_lift.tooltip: Generates a ramping lift instead of lifting the extruder directly upwards. The travel is split into two phases: the ramp and the standard horizontal travel. This option helps reduce stringing.

prusa.filament_travel_slope.label: Ramping slope angle
prusa.filament_travel_slope.tooltip: Slope of the ramp in the initial phase of the travel.

prusa.filament_seam_gap_distance.label: Seam gap distance
prusa.filament_seam_gap_distance.tooltip: The distance between the endpoints of a closed loop perimeter. Positive values will shorten and interrupt the loop slightly to reduce the seam. Negative values will extend the loop, causing the endpoints to overlap slightly. When percents are used, the distance is derived from the nozzle diameter. Set to zero to disable this feature.

prusa.default_print.label: Default Print Preset
prusa.default_print.tooltip: Name or ID of print preset to use as default when this printer preset is selected.

prusa.default_material.label: Default Material Preset
prusa.default_material.tooltip: Name or ID of material preset to use as default when this print preset is selected.

prusa.filament_change_time.label: Filament change time
prusa.filament_change_time.tooltip: Time required for a single filament change. On a printer with multiple tools this is the time required for a single toolchange to take place. On a printer with multi-material upgrade, this is the time required to unload and load a new filament.

prusa.filament_ramming_temperature_delta.label: Ramming temperature variation
prusa.filament_ramming_temperature_delta.tooltip: Temperature difference to be applied right before ramming. The value can be negative.

prusa.filament_ramming_initial_delay.label: Pause before ramming
prusa.filament_ramming_initial_delay.tooltip: Time in seconds that the printer will remain idle before ramming, allowing the melt zone temperature to equalize.

prusa.first_layer_solid_infill_speed.label: First layer solid infill speed
prusa.first_layer_solid_infill_speed.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to the solid infill print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the solid infill speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

prusa.first_layer_perimeter_speed.label: First layer perimeter speed
prusa.first_layer_perimeter_speed.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to the perimeter print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the perimeter speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

prusa.first_layer_external_perimeter_spe.label: First layer perimeter speed
prusa.first_layer_external_perimeter_spe.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to the external perimeter print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the external perimeter speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

prusa.first_layer_support_material_speed.label: First layer support material speed
prusa.first_layer_support_material_speed.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to any support print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the support material speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

prusa.first_layer_top_solid_infill_speed.label: First layer top solid infill speed
prusa.first_layer_top_solid_infill_speed.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to any top solid print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the top solid infill speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

prusa.first_layer_gap_fill_speed.label: First layer gap fill speed
prusa.first_layer_gap_fill_speed.tooltip: If expressed as absolute value in mm/s, this speed will be applied to any gap fill print moves of the first layer. If expressed as a percentage (for example: 40%) it will be a percantage of the gap fill speed. Note that 0 means that the "First layer speed" value will be used.

prusa.enable_pressure_advance_during_ram.label: Enable pressure advance during ramming
prusa.enable_pressure_advance_during_ram.tooltip: Check to enable pressure advance during ramming.

prusa.support_material_first_layer_densi.label: First layer density
prusa.support_material_first_layer_densi.tooltip: Density of the first support layer.

prusa.support_material_first_layer_expan.label: First layer expansion
prusa.support_material_first_layer_expan.tooltip: Expansion of the support first layer to improve adhesion to print bed.

prusa.stuck_filament_detection.label: Supports stuck filament monitoring configuration
prusa.stuck_filament_detection.tooltip: Enable, if the firmware supports configuring the stuck filament detection via the M591 gcode.

prusa.default_tool_print.label: Default Tool Print Preset
prusa.default_tool_print.tooltip: Name or ID of tool print preset to use as default when this print preset is selected.
